# Forensic Dossier — IONOS Group SE (IOS.DE)

> **Identity correction (read first).** The screener's peer-group file labels IOS.DE as "Intershop Communications AG," a tiny German B2B e-commerce software vendor. That is wrong. IOS.DE is **IONOS Group SE**, the Montabaur-based web-hosting, domains, productivity and cloud-infrastructure company that United Internet and Warburg Pincus floated on the Frankfurt exchange in February 2023. Every hard number in the screener block — a share price near €26.6, revenue of about €1.32 billion in 2025, roughly €645–770 million of net debt, free cash flow in the low-€300-millions — matches IONOS, not the €33-million-revenue, loss-making Intershop. The valuation that follows is built on IONOS. The "Buffett fair value €59.7" and "143% margin of safety" in the screener are products of a mismatched peer set and should be discounted heavily.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC

The story management tells has been remarkably consistent, and the consistency is itself the headline. IONOS sells the unglamorous plumbing of small-business web presence — domains, hosting, email, simple website builders — and, increasingly, cloud compute and AI-assisted tools, to a captive base of nearly 7 million customers. Through 2025 and into the first quarter of 2026 the pitch evolved from "steady subscription grower" to "steady subscription grower now bolting artificial intelligence onto a captive base." Chief Financial Officer Patrik Heider framed the core ambition plainly on the Q1 2026 call: "You need to deliver top line. EBITDA growth needs to be bigger than top-line growth" — grow revenue mid-to-high single digits while squeezing margin out faster.

Two structural changes reshaped the reported picture. First, the AdTech business (Sedo, the domain-marketplace unit) was classified as discontinued and effectively exited — its revenue fell about 97% year over year in 2025. This is the single most important thing to understand about the "minus 15.6% revenue" figure in our screener: it is a disposal artifact, not organic shrinkage. The continuing business grew roughly 5–6% in 2025 and is guided to about 7% in 2026. Second, AI moved from side-note to centerpiece: management now claims AI contributed about 20% of *additional* revenue in 2025 and expects roughly 50% in 2026 and 80% by 2028, anchored by new products such as an "AI Receptionist" (8,600-plus orders, about €30 monthly revenue per user) and the "IONOS Momentum" knowledge-hub platform.

## 2. CLAIMS vs FINANCIALS (forensic)

| Management claim | The actual numbers | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| "Profitability at record levels" (FY2025) | Adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization (EBITDA) of €485M, up 18.5%; margin expanded from 32.8% to 36.8% | **Holds.** The screener's "gross margin 57%, expanding" and "net margin 17%" corroborate a genuinely profitable, improving business. |
| "EBITDA growth bigger than top-line growth" | FY2025 revenue +5.5%, adjusted EBITDA +18.5% — EBITDA grew more than 3x faster than sales | **Holds, emphatically.** The cleanest evidence the operating-leverage thesis is working. |
| Strong customer momentum | Net adds nearly doubled, from 160,000 (2024) to 310,000 (2025); a record 180,000 added in Q1 2026 to reach 6.81M | **Holds.** The screener's EPS path (€0.44 in 2021 to €1.63 in 2025, ~39% five-year compound rate) is consistent with a widening, more profitable base. |
| Free cash flow improving | Q1 2026 free cash flow after leases €96M vs €59M a year earlier; trailing-twelve-month free cash flow €323M | **Holds.** Free-cash-flow margin of about 21% is strong for the sector. |
| AI is a needle-mover | ~20% of *additional* revenue in 2025, guided to ~50% in 2026 | **Unverified / forward-looking.** The €30-per-user AI Receptionist is early (8,600 orders against 6.8M customers is a rounding error today). Option value, not base case. |

The one place the narrative runs *richer than the numbers justify* is the AI revenue ramp. Everything else — margins, cash, customers — is backed by hard results.

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

**Stable-to-rising, in a measured, deliberately unflashy register.** Across the FY2025 and Q1 2026 calls management speaks with the calm of a company hitting its own targets. The confidence shows up not in superlatives but in reaffirmed guidance and concrete operating metrics (churn steady around 1% monthly; average revenue per user inching from €16.70 to €16.80). When pressed on the new AI products the tone turns more promotional — Heider called the company's position in "agentic AI" a "huge USP" (unique selling point) given the installed base — but on the financial mechanics he stays disciplined. There is no defensive pivot to cost-cutting language; the framing stays offensive (invest, expand margin, acquire).

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

**Medium-to-High.** IONOS reaffirmed full-year 2026 guidance on the Q1 call (about 7% constant-currency revenue growth, around €530M adjusted EBITDA, a 37–38% margin) rather than nudging it, and 2025 landed on a record-margin year as promised. The screener shows a beat rate of roughly 4 of 6 quarters (about 67%) — solid, not flawless. The medium-term targets (double-digit group revenue growth, 20% cloud growth, a 40% EBITDA margin) are more aspirational and lean on the AI ramp materializing; management has not yet had to be held to them. The score reflects a team that delivers on the near-in numbers and is appropriately vaguer on the multi-year stretch goals.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

Analysts circled three soft spots, and management deflected each:
- **Average-revenue-per-user growth.** UBS pushed on why per-user revenue is essentially flat year over year against a ~5% target. Heider attributed it to mix (new-customer dilution and currency) — reasonable, but it concedes today's pricing power is thin (price increases contribute only about 1 percentage point).
- **Hardware-cost inflation on capital spending.** Goldman Sachs pressed on rising hardware prices; Heider was "non-committal," conceding capital expenditure will run "toward the upper end" of the €75–85M range.
- **Capital allocation and the sovereign-AI "gigafactory."** On both a possible large AI-infrastructure build and on shareholder returns for the second half of 2026, Heider declined specifics, saying guidance would come "in the second half year." He also signaled appetite for "a bigger acquisition than plenty of smaller ones" and confirmed the company is "already active in discussions" — a watch-item, since a large debt-funded deal would change the risk profile.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

🟢 Margin expansion outpacing revenue by 3-to-1 — the operating-leverage thesis is proven, not promised.
🟢 Record customer adds and stable ~1% churn — the subscription base is sticky and growing.
🟢 Free cash flow nearly doubled year over year in the quarter; balance sheet moderate at ~1.3x net-debt-to-EBITDA.
🟢 Returns capital via buyback (a ~€37M / ~1% program completed March 2026) and explicitly prefers buybacks to dividends — sensible for a controlled company.
🔴 The AI revenue ramp (50% of incremental revenue this year) is the load-bearing growth claim and is largely unbooked.
🔴 Pricing power is thin — per-user revenue is roughly flat; growth is volume-led, harder to sustain at scale.
🔴 Management is openly hunting a "bigger acquisition," and the fixed-rate debt (4.7%) matures end-2026 and must be refinanced into a higher-rate world.
🔴 Free float is only ~36%; United Internet (with Warburg Pincus historically) controls the company — minority holders ride alongside a controlling parent whose interests may diverge.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The quiet but important shift is the AdTech exit: by discontinuing Sedo, management cleaned the reported business down to two higher-quality engines — Web Presence & Productivity (about 83–84% of revenue, growing 6–8%) and Cloud Solutions (about 14%, growing high single digits with public cloud up 16% and guided above 20%). That makes the company easier to value on a sum-of-the-parts basis and signals focus on the recurring, higher-margin core. A second subtle tell: the language around a large acquisition and an unspecified sovereign-AI "gigafactory" build hints the next 12 months could bring a capital-allocation event — potentially accretive, potentially balance-sheet-stretching. The controlling-shareholder structure is the unspoken backdrop to every capital decision.

## 8. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

**Classification: STRENGTHENING.** This is a genuinely good small/mid-cap compounder — expanding margins, growing cash, a sticky subscription base — trading at a modest multiple (about 12x price-to-free-cash-flow) largely because the headline revenue line was distorted by the AdTech disposal and because it is a thinly-floated, parent-controlled European name that screens as "deep value" almost by accident.

The single most important thing the director must weigh before sizing: **there is no hard catalyst.** The discount is real, but it is the kind that compounds slowly as margins expand and cash builds, not the kind that snaps shut on a dated event. The one event that *could* force a re-rating — a take-private/squeeze-out by United Internet, or a transformational acquisition — is unannounced and speculative. Size this as a patient quality-at-a-reasonable-price holding, not an event-driven trade, and watch the end-2026 debt refinancing and any large-deal announcement.

**Moat:** narrow but real — switching costs and scale economics in commodity hosting (a domain/email/website bundle 6.8 million customers are reluctant to migrate), reinforced by brand and a low-cost European data-center footprint. It is *widening*, not eroding: returns on invested capital (~14%) and margins are rising, not falling. The secular backdrop is mixed — website-builder and basic-hosting commoditization is a slow headwind, but the AI-tooling layer is at least as much an opportunity as a threat, so terminal-value risk is manageable rather than structural.
